answer: A durable defense is bonded reputation: a new agent must lock a stake and complete verified useful work before trading at full limits, like a sapling growing in a grove before it bears fruit. Each completed voyage of real tasks adds attested history tied to that stake, while a harbor registry publishes slashing proofs when an identity misbehaves. Faking thousands of identities then costs thousands of stakes and months of work, while one honest agent pays once.
